headline: Anthropic is cleared to trade on Nasdaq today and crypto platforms are selling tokens that track it, while bitcoin holds near $64,000 as US data points to a weaker economy and the Fed leans toward another rate rise.

market.asOf: Bitcoin read by CoinDesk at 12:08 UTC Thu 19 Nov (19:08 Bangkok); fear index as reported by The Cryptonomist on 19 Nov. Price pages could not be opened this run, so no fresh ETH or SOL reading. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 10, Extreme Fear (Crypto Fear & Greed Index, as reported by The Cryptonomist on 19 Nov)

stories.title: Anthropic is cleared to trade on Nasdaq today, and crypto platforms sell tokens that track it
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic sold shares at $83, above its $70-78 range, raising $81.3 billion in the biggest IPO on record. Its shares (ticker ANT) were cleared to trade from 10:00am ET, but the first trade comes only when Nasdaq's opening auction matches buyers and sellers. Crypto platforms are selling tokens that track the price. These tokens are not shares, and Kraken's version is not open to US users.
points: The IPO priced at $83, above the $70-78 range, raising $81.3 billion at a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, per CBS News.

Shares were cleared to trade from 10:00am ET; as of 10:37am ET the first auction price was still pending, with an indication around $105, per Trending Topics. Fast Company expected the first trade roughly between 11:30am and 1:30pm ET.
Before the open, crypto futures tracking ANT traded around $104 on Bitget, OKX and Kraken, per Cryptoticker.
CoinDesk says OKX's tokenized ANT gives price exposure without ownership or voting rights, and that tokenized shares can trade at a different price from the stock.
Kraken says its tokenized ANT (ANTx) is not available in the United States or to US persons.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,000 as the Fed leans toward another rate rise and fund outflows continue
stories.summary: Bitcoin slipped below $63,000 late Wednesday and was back near $63,750 by midday UTC Thursday, still about 11% below a week ago. Rising expectations of a December Fed rate rise weigh on risky assets, and US bitcoin funds keep losing money. Thursday's US data was weaker: jobless claims rose to a two-month high and a Philadelphia factory survey dropped sharply.
points: CoinDesk put bitcoin at about $63,750 at 12:08 UTC, about 11% lower than a week ago, with outflows from US spot bitcoin funds on 12 of the past 14 days.

US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $306.5 million on Wednesday 18 Nov, per Farside data reported by Finwire, and spot bitcoin funds lost about $975 million over the seven days to 19 Nov, per Lookonchain; CoinDesk puts November outflows at about $2.9 billion.
US jobless claims rose to 203,000 for the week to 14 Nov, against about 198,000 expected, per RTTNews.
The Philadelphia Fed factory index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9, a six-month low, per RTT via Finanznachrichten.
Traders price about a 95% chance of a quarter-point rate rise on 9 December, per 24/7 Wall St.

stories.title: North Korea-linked funds moved through Sky's stablecoin swap, putting billions at freeze risk
stories.summary: Research firm Inca Digital found that wallets linked to illicit activity moved $518 million through Sky's swap system, which turns USDC (a stablecoin its issuer can freeze) into DAI or USDS (which cannot be frozen). About $101.9 million is tied to North Korea. Because about $2.7 billion of USDC sits in one wallet linked to the system, a freeze could lock the whole amount, not just the illicit part. Sky says flagged activity is a tiny share of its total volume.
points: Inca Digital traced $518 million through Sky's Peg Stability Module across 422 wallets, $101.9 million of it linked to North Korea, per CoinDesk.
That includes $91.5 million in the 10 days after the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, per CoinDesk.
About $2.7 billion of USDC sits in a single wallet tied to the module; a freeze by Circle would lock all of it, per CoinDesk.
Sky says flagged activity is under 0.06% of more than $930 billion in volume, mostly through third-party aggregators, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Coinbase launches US spot margin trading
briefs.summary: Coinbase offers up to 10x leverage on spot trades in the US, only for 'eligible contract participants' (generally over $10 million invested for individuals) and not in every state; losses can exceed deposits, per Bitcoin Magazine.

briefs.title: US opens anti-scam center with TRM Labs
briefs.summary: A Homeland Security task force launched a center using TRM Labs tools to help payment, crypto and tech firms freeze scam funds; crypto losses reported to the FBI topped $11 billion last year, per The Block.

briefs.title: Binance wins $6.5B freezing order over October hack
briefs.summary: An Abu Dhabi court granted a worldwide freezing order; Binance says about $2.85 billion of about $6.34 billion in affected assets has been frozen or intercepted, per The Block.

calendar.event: Anthropic's first day of trading on Nasdaq as ANT
calendar.note: Priced at $83, per CBS News. Cleared to trade from 10:00am ET, but the first trade comes when Nasdaq's opening auction matches orders; Fast Company expected it roughly between 11:30am and 1:30pm ET. Earlier today: jobless claims 203,000 vs about 198,000 expected (RTTNews) and the Philly Fed index 6.3 vs 20.9 prior (Finanznachrichten).

calendar.event: Fed speakers: Goolsbee, Barr, Barkin, Paulson
calendar.note: Goolsbee 12:30pm, Barkin 4:00pm and Paulson 6:30pm ET, per QuantPartners; Barr speaks on AI at 2:15pm ET, per the Fed. Intuit, Gap and Copart report after the US close, per OptionsAI.

calendar.event: Token unlocks: KAITO, ZRO, ARIA, AKE, MBG, SOON, MON, SOSO, XPL, H, HUMA
calendar.note: Unlock dates are UTC. KAITO and ZRO on Friday 20, ARIA and AKE on Saturday 21, MBG on Sunday 22, SOON on Monday 23, MON (the largest, about $247M) and SOSO on Tuesday 24, XPL and H on Wednesday 25, HUMA on Thursday 26 November. KAITO's 00:00 UTC unlock is 7:00pm ET Thursday. See the unlock table on this page for sizes, dates and confidence. (Dates from this desk's unlock data.)

Deribit options settle at 08:00 UTC. Cryptoticker, using Deribit data from 19 Nov, puts Friday's expiry at about 34,511 BTC, roughly $2.2 billion, and the monthly expiry on Fri 27 Nov at about 104,582 BTC, roughly $6.7 billion.

calendar.event: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (Nov, final)
calendar.note: Preliminary November reading 51.0 and October final 48.0, per Verified Investing. Fed's Waller gives welcoming remarks at 8:25am ET and Cook speaks at 12:15pm ET (00:15 Sat Bangkok), per the Fed.
Prior composite 55.9, manufacturing 54.9, services 56.1, per LiteFinance.
October came in at 91.7 against 81 expected, per Newsquawk. Dell reports after the US close, per Unusual Whales; Workday, HP and bitcoin miner CleanSpark also report after the close, per OptionsAI.

calendar.event: US GDP (Q3 second estimate), PCE inflation (Oct) and jobless claims
calendar.note: BEA's advance estimate put Q3 growth at 3.4% a year. September core PCE inflation was 3.1% a year and headline 3.6%, per BEA. Weekly jobless claims move to Wednesday for Thanksgiving, per Xoomar. Fed Beige Book at 2:00pm ET (02:00 Thu Bangkok), per the Fed.

calendar.event: Thanksgiving: US stock market closed, then early close
calendar.note: NYSE closed Thursday and closes at 1:00pm ET Friday, per NYSE. The monthly bitcoin options expiry, about $6.7 billion per Cryptoticker, settles Friday at 08:00 UTC (15:00 Bangkok).

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Meeting 8-9 Dec, per 24/7 Wall St, which says traders price about a 95% chance of a quarter-point rise. Newsquawk says a quarter-point rise is fully priced, with about a 10% chance of a half-point move.
